clue.text: A topless dominatrix pops up to provide rough ideas

indicators.note: up here means in a disordered state, as when things are 'up', so the letters before it get rearranged
topless means the word dominatrix loses its top, i.e. its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of dominatrix

explanation.surface: A dominatrix without her top appears, supplying vague notions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts D from 'dominatrix'; what remains plus 'pops' is rearranged, signalled by 'up'. 'pops up' reads as one phrase, but 'pops' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximations are estimates that are close but not exact, which is what rough ideas are.

clue.text: Star finally stripping naked for Playboy

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Star
stripping means the word naked loses its outer layers, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes everything off for a men's magazine shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: R ends 'Star'; 'stripping' takes the outer letters off NAKED, leaving AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man about town, the same type as a playboy.

clue.text: Disappointing change in Raleigh Cycling — with brownish-yellow colour trimming handlebars at first

indicators.note: Cycling means the letters of the coin go round, the end letters moved to the front

parts.note: Raleigh is a US city, so a piece of American change is a dime

indicators.note: trimming means a letter is cut away from the colour word

parts.note: ochre is a brownish-yellow earth pigment

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of handlebars

explanation.surface: A disappointing alteration to a Raleigh bicycle: brownish-yellow paint and trimmed handlebars.
explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh is a bicycle brand in the surface but the capital of North Carolina in the wordplay. 'Cycling' turns DIME into MEDI; 'trimming' takes H (first of 'handlebars') out of OCHRE, leaving OCRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is only middling in quality, and so it lets you down.

clue.text: They'd put saddles on in fancy stores — bolts, essentially, must go in the middle

indicators.note: must go in the middle says the single letter is placed inside the rearranged word
fancy here is an adjective meaning elaborate or reworked, so the letters of stores are rearranged
essentially points to the essence, the central letter, of the word bolts

explanation.surface: Saddling up in a smart shop, while the horses bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges STORES to OSTERS; 'essentially' gives L, the centre of 'bolts', and 'must go in the middle' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostlers were the stablemen at inns who looked after travellers' horses, including tacking them up.

clue.text: Cycle unfinished — in India one comes in two pieces

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cycle is a bike
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An incomplete bicycle in India arrives in two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a swimsuit made of two separate parts, top and bottom.

clue.text: Meeting to study viral infection with nurse and chemical engineer

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
flu, influenza, is a viral infection
EN is an Enrolled Nurse
CE is short for chemical engineer

explanation.surface: A meeting to look at a viral outbreak, attended by a nurse and a chemical engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A confluence is a coming together, especially of rivers, so a meeting or junction.

clue.text: Happy to see revamp

parts.note: to feel up is to be happy or in high spirits
to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to see a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something is to bring it up to date, a modernising overhaul much like a revamp.

clue.text: Wine — mostly very strong on board SS Enterprise and Endeavour?

definitions.note: the plural answer is defined by two examples, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: on board means the other letters go aboard, inside, the ship's prefix SS
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Pinot is a wine grape and its wine
FF is fortissimo, very loud or strong in music

explanation.surface: Drinking strong wine aboard two ships named Enterprise and Endeavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts T from PINOT. Enterprise and Endeavour look like ships but are TV series: Star Trek: Enterprise spun off from Star Trek, Endeavour from the detective drama Inspector Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both shows are derivative series built from an earlier hit, which is what a spin-off is.

clue.text: Good time girl with northern charm ignoring an orthodox viewpoint

parts.note: a good time is fun
dame is an informal word for a woman or girl

indicators.note: ignoring means the word an is left out of the charm word

parts.note: a talisman is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: A party girl with Northern charm turns her back on strict beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops AN from TALISMAN, leaving TALISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentalism is strict adherence to the basic tenets of a faith, a rigidly orthodox outlook.

clue.text: Voluntary leave without payment to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the payment word is placed at the start

parts.note: something given without payment is free
to leave something to someone, bequeath it, is to will it

explanation.surface: Unpaid leave, as a starting offer, taken voluntarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' looks like time off work, but here it is the verb to bequeath.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-will as an adjective describes something done by choice, uncompelled, that is voluntarily.

clue.text: Popular female soldier's child

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a soldier ant is a kind of ant; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman soldier's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a baby or very young child; in law it means any minor.

clue.text: Dog's regular I see for say going on supplement in addition to routine courses

indicators.note: going on says the piece after is attached onto the supplement word

parts.note: an extra is a supplement or add-on
a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: for says one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: taken as the word itself
EG, for example, is what say means here
IC, the letters, read out as 'I see'

explanation.surface: A dog's usual diet now has a supplement added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' marks the swap of one abbreviation for another inside 'regular', with 'I see' read as two letters; 'going on' places the dog and that word after the supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracurricular activities happen outside or beyond the normal timetable of school or college lessons.

clue.text: Reading about award

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a citation is a formal commendation, as for bravery

explanation.surface: A reading concerning an award, as at a prize ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' could be the town, but here it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitation is a performance reading of a text aloud to an audience.

clue.text: Heroin addict abandoning us for £1

parts.note: smack is slang for heroin

indicators.note: abandoning means the word us is left out of the addict word

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: A heroin addict leaves us, all for a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops US from USER, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacker is slang for a pound sterling (or a dollar), a single unit of money.

clue.text: Some critics pan Dexy's material

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some critics slate the material of Dexys Midnight Runners, the 1980s band.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandex is a stretchy synthetic fabric, so a type of material.

clue.text: Perhaps Charlotte, North Carolina's filling ministers' time away

indicators.note: filling says the state abbreviation goes inside the other word
away means the time letter is taken out of the ministers word

parts.note: priests are ministers of religion
NC is the abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: Charlotte, the North Carolina city, filling ministers' free time.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte is a North Carolina city in the surface but a royal here. 'away' removes the time letter and 'filling' puts the state inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Charlotte of Wales is a British princess, so an example of one.

clue.text: They might draw the line at this in Stockley Park

definitions.text: They might draw the line at this in Stockley Park

parts.words: They might draw the line at this in Stockley Park
parts.note: Stockley Park, west London, houses the Premier League's video referee hub, where officials draw lines on replays to judge players' positions

explanation.surface: People in an office park might refuse to tolerate this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw the line at' means refuse to accept, but here VAR officials literally draw lines on the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Offside calls in football are checked by VAR officials who draw lines across the pitch to compare positions.

clue.text: About 100 tons of copper batteries fly out all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hefty load of copper batteries fly out in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's famous monument is a copper-clad colossus whose skin alone weighs tens of tons.

clue.text: River around large town with back of dinghy leaving wake

indicators.note: around says the river goes round the other piece

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs the town word

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of dinghy

explanation.surface: On a river near a town, a dinghy leaves its wake behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' looks like a boat's trail but is the verb, to rouse. 'leaving' drops the dinghy's last letter from the town; 'around' wraps the Devon river round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite and to wake both mean to rouse or stir something into activity.

clue.text: Quote work from the east — it's imaginative

indicators.note: from the east means read from right to left in an across answer, so backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
OP, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A quotation from an eastern work, praised as imaginative.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic writing is full of creative imagery and expressive imagination.

clue.text: Perhaps Stallone's accepting old agents' bill, initially in a friendly manner

indicators.note: accepting says the name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Sylvester Stallone is known as Sly, so he is an example of a Sly
the CIA is the US agency of intelligence agents

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of bill

explanation.surface: Stallone graciously takes an old bill from secret agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sociably means doing it in an outgoing, companionable, friendly way.

clue.text: Without a shred of doubt, who made Thomas crooked

indicators.note: Without says that letter is removed from the author's name

parts.note: the Rev. W. Awdry created Thomas the Tank Engine

indicators.note: a shred of means just a tiny bit, the first letter, of doubt

explanation.surface: Undoubtedly, whoever made Thomas was crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes D (a shred of 'doubt') out of AWDRY. Thomas the Tank Engine is a children's book and TV character.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry describes something askew, out of line, that is, crooked.

clue.text: Wally or Edward, briefly mixed

parts.note: a wally is a British slang word for a fool, an ass
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Wally or Edward, a muddled short list of names.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of various kinds, mixed together.

clue.text: Worry safecracker's opening lock

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of safecracker's

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A safecracker frets over opening a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is anxiety or strain, much the same as worry.
